transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-09 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Samir Patel, Leah Gomez (Redwood); Tom Liu, Priya Nair, Evan Brooks (NexaHealth)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate keeping to the weekly cadence. quick check - is this still a good time?
[00:08] Tom: Yeah this works, thanks. we're coming out of a sprint so timing is fine.
[00:12] Leah: Cool. I put the agenda in the chat — onboarding status, infra access, smoke test numbers, next steps.
[00:19] Priya: got it. i'll flag up front— we hit a blocker yesterday with the VPC peering, some firewall rules need to be loosened.
[00:27] Samir: okay thanks, that'll be one of the action items. Evan, anything from security?
[00:31] Evan: yeah quick note — we'll need the SOC2 artifact set and a bit more detail on audit logging. also confirm how KMS will be used, whether we call out a bring-your-own-key flow.
[00:43] Leah: yep we support BYOK; for the POC we can test with a test KMS ARN and then switch over. small caveat: for hosted we do envelope encryption and there's an audit log tie-in, for dedicated we can give more direct KMS integration.
[00:58] Tom: good. Priya, can you summarize where we are on providing the KMS info?
[01:03] Priya: i have the KMS account owner identified, just need to get the ARN and a service account. expecting to push that today or tomorrow.
[01:12] Samir: great. Leah, can you quickly run through the smoke test numbers you ran last week? I know you ran a few prompts on the staging cluster.
[01:20] Leah: sure. caveat— the staging run used our smaller model variant (redwood-mini was the label in the job) and stock quantization so it's not final. but rough numbers: average token throughput was about 480 tokens/sec on a single A100 equivalent instance, p95 latency at 512 token context was ~420ms, p99 was spiky up to 1.2s. those p99 spikes appear when KV cache misses happen — as in the initial prefix hasn't been warmed.
[01:48] Priya: that p99 is a bit higher than our target, we're trying to hit p99 under 500ms for UI use. is that realistic on your dedicated config?
[01:58] Leah: yes on dedicated with aggressive prefix caching and tuned batching we expect p99 ~350-450ms at similar load. we need to run the dedicated benchmark with your actual prompt mix.
[02:12] Samir: also worth noting cost tradeoffs — dedicated will be higher baseline but lower per-token at scale, hosted is lower ops. Tom, what matters more for you right now?
[02:23] Tom: predictability and data controls — if dedicated gets us consistent latency and we can meet cost targets, we lean dedicated. but we need the numbers to justify.
[02:33] Evan: and auditability — we can't send PHI to a multitenant endpoint without certain DLP controls. we need to see how logs are retained and who has access.
[02:44] Leah: understood. for audit logs we can push a subset to your SIEM via a secured webhook; for dedicated we can provide instance-level logs and longer retention windows.
[02:55] Priya: any rough ETA on the dedicated benchmark run?
[02:58] Leah: I can schedule it as soon as VPC peering + KMS creds are available — ideally tomorrow (2026-12-10) if you can provide peering today. but realistically we'll aim for 2026-12-14 for the full run.
[03:12] Tom: okay, we'll prioritize getting the peering and firewall changes. Evan will own the firewall whitelists.
[03:17] Evan: yep I'll open a ticket with infra and get back with the CIDRs by EOD.
[03:22] Samir: perfect. quick question on the peering — do you need a dedicated subnet range or are we doing shared?
[03:27] Evan: we'll do a dedicated peered subnet for the POC, keeps routes cleaner.
[03:31] Leah: great, please send the CIDR and the expected egress IPs — we'll add them to our side.
[03:37] Priya: another thing — we saw some tokenization mismatches in the smoke tests, sometimes the length estimates were off which skews batching. is there a recommended tokenizer or preprocessor you prefer?
[03:48] Leah: our runtime expects UTF-8 and we recommend you normalize whitespace and strip embedded html. tokenizer is compatible with GPT-like BPE; we can share a snippet in the repo. small transcription note: sometimes the tokenizer name got garbled in our notes as 'g p t b p e' — but we'll provide the exact package.
[04:06] Samir: i'll include that in the follow-up bundle with the sample script.
[04:10] Tom: great. can we talk briefly about regression checks? we want to ensure quality doesn't drop with quantized models.
[04:17] Leah: yes — we run evals against your prompt set. for this POC we'll run a baseline on the float model and compare to int8/int4 quantized variants. we surface rouge/lexical metrics plus a small human review sample. if you have a bench set, please attach.
[04:33] Priya: we cleaned up a 200-example set yesterday; i'll drop it into the shared drive.
[04:39] Leah: perfect. that will speed things up.
[04:42] Samir: on procurement/contracting — Samir here — quick update: legal asked for an updated SOW reflecting the dedicated burst capacity option. i'll revise and send draft by Monday (2026-12-13).
[04:56] Tom: sounds good. question — about retention and deletion for the POC, can we have a short retention policy for the hosted logs?
[05:04] Leah: yes we can set retention to 7 days for the POC, and longer retention for dedicated if needed — that's configurable in the console.
[05:12] Evan: please include that in the SOW language for clarity.
[05:16] Samir: will do.
[05:18] [06:00] (short side conversation — background noise)
[06:20] Priya: on metrics — Leah, can you confirm what exact metric names you'll populate in the dashboard? we want latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, model version, and KV cache hit rate.
[06:33] Leah: yes those are available. also we'll add per-route cost estimates and a per-request breakdown of tokenized length. note that KV cache hit rate occasionally shows false negatives if prefix normalization differs.
[06:48] Priya: ok we'll standardize normalization.
[06:51] Tom: do you have a recommended batching policy for interactive UI with high concurrency?
[06:58] Leah: for lower latency UI we recommend smaller max batch size (e.g., 8) and lower batch wait (e.g., 10ms). that keeps p99 down but increases compute. we can try adaptive batching during the benchmark.
[07:12] Samir: and we'll include cost simulation for batch size tradeoffs.
[07:16] Evan: security question — for BYOK flow, how is key rotation handled? we need to ensure rotation doesn't break cached tokens or sessions.
[07:26] Leah: rotation is handled at the envelope layer; rotation won't invalidate existing KV cache entries. we'll send the KMS rotation doc after the call.
[07:35] Priya: can you also clarify network egress — do you do any third-party calls that might hit external endpoints?
[07:42] Leah: no outbound calls besides optional telemetry to your SIEM if configured; model execution is local to the cluster.
[07:49] Tom: that's good.
[07:51] [08:00] Samir: quick recap so we capture commitments — Priya will send KMS ARN and service account by 2026-12-11; Evan to provide CIDRs by EOD 2026-12-09; Leah to schedule dedicated benchmark for 2026-12-14; Samir to send SOW/pricing by 2026-12-13. anything to add?
[08:12] Priya: add that we'll share the 200-example eval set today.
[08:16] Tom: and we'll look for the onboarding run results in the shared folder.
[08:20] Leah: i'll share initial benchmark templates and a runbook after the call — link in chat.
[08:26] Samir: cool. any final Qs?
[08:30] Evan: one more — can you provide an example of the audit log schema? we need to map fields to our SIEM.
[08:38] Leah: yes, example schema will be attached. it includes timestamp, request_id, model_version, route, token_count, user_id (obfuscated) and event_type. we'll redact PHI by default unless you opt in for raw logs.
[08:55] Priya: thanks. that's all from me.
[09:00] Tom: same, good sync.
[09:05] Samir: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and SOW. talk soon.

End of transcript. Notes: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., tokenizer name split), natural filler words preserved. Files referenced: shared drive link, bench set, SOW draft, benchmark runbook (links in chat).
